title: A Highly Accurate Fast Decoding Framework for QLDPC codes Accelerated by Noise Perturbation and Ensemble Decoding
abstract: A well-balanced decoder has been central to the development of modern fault-tolerant quantum computing. However, the inherent topologies of quantum error correcting codes can limit the performance of many well-studied decoding algorithms. In this work, we introduce Noise Assisted Ensemble Decoding (NAED), a highly accurate decoding framework with a significant advantage in real-time speed. NAED constructs an ensemble of Tanner forests, obtained as acyclic subgraphs of the original Tanner graph, and performs exact inference on each Tanner forest using a lightweight dynamic programming algorithm. The forest construction is guided by synthetic soft information derived jointly from the measured syndrome and channel statistics, with controlled noise perturbations generating diverse yet informative decoding matrix column orderings for the Tanner forest construction across the ensemble. Our benchmark results show that the proposed synthetic soft information-driven construction and inference on the Tanner forests can achieve improved or comparable decoding performances to the state-of-the-art decoding solutions, such as BP+OSD$0$, while also providing orders-of-magnitude improvements in per-round decoding speed under circuit-level noise.
summary: This paper introduces Noise Assisted Ensemble Decoding (NAED), a novel framework designed to decode Quantum Low-Density Parity Check (QLDPC) codes efficiently. NAED constructs an ensemble of Tanner forests using synthetic soft information derived from noise measurements. It demonstrates that this method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while providing massive speedups, crucial for practical quantum error correction.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a decoding framework for Quantum Low-Density Parity Check (QLDPC) codes that is both highly accurate and significantly faster than existing state-of-the-art methods.
main_result: The proposed Noise Assisted Ensemble Decoding (NAED) achieves performance comparable to the best decoders while offering orders-of-magnitude improvements in per-round decoding speed, making it suitable for real-time quantum computation.
method: NAED constructs an ensemble of Tanner forests by guiding their construction with synthetic soft information derived from syndrome measurements and channel statistics, followed by exact inference via dynamic programming on each forest.
model_or_system: The work focuses on fault-tolerant quantum computing using QLDPC codes. The analysis involves simulating decoding performance under circuit-level Pauli noise models applied to the code structure defined by sparse Deterministic Encoding Matrices (DEMs).
key_observables: Decoding performance (Logical Error Rate, $p_L$) and per-round decoding speed.
important_parameters: Circuit noise rate ($p$), noise scaling parameter ($	au$), and the weight of columns in the DEM matrix ($	ext{wt}(D:q)$).
main_assumptions: The framework addresses the Degenerate Quantum Maximum Likelihood Decoding (DQMLD) problem, which existing classical decoders fail to solve due to code degeneracies.
figures_summary: Figures compare Logical Error Rates for Surface Codes and BB codes using various decoder strategies (BP+OTF vs NAED) across varying circuit noise rates, demonstrating NAED's superior performance.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of current decoders regarding QLDPC degeneracies. It then details the NAED framework, which uses synthetic soft information and ensemble construction on Tanner forests for exact inference. Finally, it validates this approach through circuit-level simulations comparing its performance against established methods like BP+OTF.
why_interesting: The focus on decoding algorithms for QLDPC codes is central to realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation, which is a major goal in theoretical physics and quantum information science.
